_meta.purpose: Name rules that tie each file of a NASA PSI file listing to rows of an experimental table by the identifier its name carries, for pipeline/raw_names.py; the suffix codes of the names with their meanings as quoted from NASA documents; and what the opened videos of each investigation showed as text on screen.
_meta.source_of_rules: The rules were written from a name-only survey of the 2026-11-14 listings (one AI agent per investigation, checked against the experimental tables) and re-applied by raw_names.py; differences from that survey are listed in _meta.differences_from_survey.
_meta.name_rule: The name of a file is the last part of its listing key with the PSI prefix ('PSI-25_Raw Data_', 'PSI-25_metadata_') removed, as spec/raw_kinds.json removes it; the extension is kept. 'where': 'folder' rules read the PSI subcategory path of the listing instead of the name.
_meta.rule_order: Rules of an investigation are tried in the order listed; within a rule every match of 'pattern' is tried from left to right; the first match that ties at least one row decides. A file that no rule ties is not tied (link level none).
_meta.tie: A match ties the rows of the rule's tables (all tables of the investigation if 'tables' is not given) at which, for every named group of the pattern that matched, the key transform of the group text is one of the values the cell transform gives for the row's cells of the field's columns. 'row_filter' keeps only rows whose cell matches a regex; 'mode' 'each_field_ties_union' ties the union of the rows that each group ties, and only if each group ties a row. 'level' is the link level of the tie; 'level_if_several_rows' replaces it when more than one row is tied.

transforms.int: the digits read as an integer (leading zeros dropped)
transforms.first5: the first five characters (cell: spaces removed first)
transforms.digits_prefix: the leading digits of the cell as an integer ('145m' -> 145)
transforms.cir: upper case, with an F put in front when the text begins with a digit
transforms.yyddd_date: five digits read as two-digit year (20YY) and day of year, as a calendar date
transforms.ymd_date: eight digits (separators dropped) read as year, month, day
transforms.ymd_yyddd: a calendar date written as two-digit year and three-digit day of year
transforms.ymd_dmon: a calendar date written as day and abbreviated month, without the year ('7-sep')
transforms.dmony_date: DDMonYYYY read as a calendar date
transforms.upper_prefix6: letters only, upper case, first six letters
transforms.ymd_cols: cells Year, Month (number or English month name, a final dot dropped) and Date as a calendar date
transforms.date: a cell written m/d/yyyy, d-Mon-yy, yyyy-MON-dd (words may follow) or yyyy-mm-dd as a calendar date
transforms.doy: the day of the year of such a date
transforms.gmt_int: the number after GMT in the cell
transforms.slash_parts_upper: the parts of the cell split at '/', upper case
transforms.each_upper: every cell of the field's columns, upper case
transforms.after_hyphen: the part of the cell after the first hyphen

levels.test: the name carries the identifier of one test (one row of the table; two rows where the table repeats an identifier)
levels.day_or_session: the name carries a day, session or set key that several rows share, or a row key that is not a test of tests.csv

_meta.suffix_rule: The suffix code of a file is the first entry of 'suffix_codes' whose pattern is found in the name (case as the entry says); a file that no entry matches has '(no suffix code)'. A meaning is a quote of 25 words or fewer from a NASA document of the investigation, confirmed in the document text on 2026-11-14 (document, PSI file id, place); 'meaning': null means that no stated meaning was found in the documents read.
_meta.video_rule: 'videos.on_screen_text' is the class that the earlier video survey gave after opening a few videos per investigation and re-viewing the frames; 'labels_seen' are the labels read on screen; 'opened' and 'with_text' count the videos opened and those that showed readings. It says what the opened videos showed, not what the other videos show.
_meta.quote_check: Every quote under 'meaning' (suffix codes and identifier meanings) was searched for in the text of its document (pdftotext, or the XML text of docx, pptx and xlsx files) after folding white space, case and typographic quotes, on 2026-11-14; all 139 quotes were found, in 38 documents of 19 investigations. Quotes not found would have been dropped.
differences_from_survey: PSI-69: 6 files that the survey tied through an identifier stated inside the opened file (FLEX-073_ResultsSummary.pdf and five others) are not tied here: the rules read names only.

PSI-101: 43 HKPData_gmt<day> files that the survey tied to days by reading the day number as a day of 2010 are not tied here (no year in the name or the cell); 2 files whose only number is a test number in running text ('more 54.zip', 'SPV of 54-7L_21 ...') are not tied here.
PSI-107: 41 'TP <number>' files that the survey tied to one test through the master sheet column 'No.' are tied to their day here (the master sheet is not in the repository).
The other 60,706 of the 60,798 files of the 19 investigations with a survey links file have the same link level, and the test-level files the same tests, as the survey.

layers.structure: sample files opened for their headers, keys or labels (spec/raw_columns.json)
layers.archive_directories: central directories of a sample of zip archives read by byte ranges (pipeline/zip_directory.py); no archive downloaded

levels.test: tied to a test by name

summary.units: bytes as the PSI listing reports them
summary.tie_by_name: A tie by name means that the name carries the identifier of that test (or day), equal to a cell of the experimental table; the content of the file was not checked.
summary.names: Of {files} listed files, {t} are tied to a test by name, {d} to a day or session, and {n} are not tied.
summary.structure: {files} sample files were opened for their headers, keys or labels; one file of a group does not show what the other files of the group hold.
summary.values: {files} files were read in full for values (raw_values.csv); no value of a raw file is used by the pipeline.
summary.archives: The directory of {a} of {all} archives was read by byte ranges without downloading them ({f} bytes fetched for {b} bytes of archives); the member names are a sample.
summary.rank: The rank of data/pipeline/retrieval_queue.csv is a fixed ordering rule (tests lacking the value, descending, then bytes of the group, ascending); it is not a priority set by the team or by NASA.
summary.not_content: None of these layers says that a file holds a quantity, nor whether its values are complete or calibrated.

raw_state_sentences._note: Fixed sentences added by pipeline/raw_gaps.py to need_gap_states.csv and to the raw_state items of the evidence packages, where videos are tied by name to tests that lack the variable. {n}: videos tied by name to these tests (a file tied to two tests counts once per test); {m}: tests with at least one such video.
raw_state_sentences.videos_tied: {n} videos are tied by name to {m} of these tests; whether the quantity can be read from them was not checked.
raw_state_sentences.videos_on_screen: Opened videos of this investigation show readings as on-screen text: {labels} ({seen}).

archive_sample_note: A sample: directories of 23 archives chosen by size class and name pattern (3 by size, then the median-size archive of the 20 largest name-pattern groups); member names were read, members were not opened.

A three-digit day token with a leading 0 after OT_, RoomT_, 'OT ', pic_info_ or 100CH4_<n>_ in the name equals the day of the year of a 'Test Date' cell.
UT_<ddd>_<ddd> in the name: both tokens equal days of the year of 'Test Date' cells; ties to the rows of both days.
A date written as eight digits in the name equals the date of a 'Test Date' cell.

No day token in the name: the first three-digit day token with a leading 0 in the listing folder (PSI subcategory) that equals the day of the year of a 'Test Date' cell; a tie by the location in the listing. Not applied to videos (their links stay by name).
